headline: High risk of prompt injection and data leakage: next-ai-draw-io can ingest files and use MCP/broad egress, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can feed untrusted content back into the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs, text, images, and draw.io XML and uses MCP; PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can therefore supply attacker-controlled content into A’s instruction-following path. No shared filesystem is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly observed, but the pathway exists in default document-processing use.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is copied or piped into next-ai-draw-io as source material, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF next-ai-draw-io treats file contents or MCP payloads as trusted instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Separate untrusted OCR output from instruction prompts.
Add a fixed delimiter and system prompt that forbids following content inside documents.
Review MCP tool inputs before execution.
Use a manual approval step before acting on extracted text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from OCR to downstream prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A explicitly handles API keys and has broad network egress; B has allowlisted egress and processes documents/images. If sensitive documents flow through both, A can transmit content to third-party model APIs and B can expose extracted text upstream. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default document workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are processed by both agents in the same workflow, extracted content can leave the local boundary.
IF next-ai-draw-io sends prompts or file contents to external model APIs, document text may be disclosed.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-sensitive sample files.
Disable external API backends for A where possible.
Use a local-only network policy for the workflow.
Redact secrets before OCR or diagram generation.
requires-engineering: enforce per-document data-class routing and DLP checks.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can run browsers and touch documents/images, but only A advertises broad egress and MCP while B’s egress is allowlisted. No shared writable filesystem or overlapping mutable resource is documented, so write-conflict risk is limited and mostly configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace, file overwrite conflicts become possible.
IF an orchestrator grants both write access to the same output directory, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run the agents sequentially instead of concurrently.
Lock shared files during writes.
Keep browser sessions isolated.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and B performs OCR/document parsing; if B’s extracted text is fed into A without verification, A can render or propagate OCR mistakes as authoritative diagram content. This is a default workflow risk, but not clearly irreversible.
conditions: IF B’s OCR output is used as direct input to A, transcription errors can cascade into diagrams.
IF downstream users trust A’s generated diagram without review, incorrect facts persist.
mitigations: Require human review of OCR text before diagram generation.
Compare OCR output against source pages for critical fields.
Mark generated diagrams as unverified drafts.
Use confidence thresholds to flag uncertain OCR spans.
requires-engineering: add validation against source-document anchors.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. A handles API keys and broad egress, but B’s compliance surface is not described, so only a limited compliance-gap risk is supportable from the profiles.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through external APIs in A, local policy may be violated.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees, the undocumented B side may fail them.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair.
Document retention settings for any external API use.
Review vendor DPAs before production use.
Log data-class handling decisions.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance attestations for both tools.
